headline_marked: Mefi's Studio AI+ 0.4: [[Agent Brain, Project Map]] and coordinated agents previewed
headline: Mefi's Studio AI+ 0.4: Agent Brain, Project Map and coordinated agents previewed
summary: A development preview of Mefi's Studio AI+ 0.4 showcases Agent Brain for task pipelines, Project Map for Git history visualization, and enhanced agent coordination.
details: Mefi's Studio AI+ is getting a significant update with version 0.4, focusing on improved visibility and coordination for AI coding agents. The development preview introduces Agent Brain, which live-views a task's pipeline, lead agent, and sub-agents, with replayable work events.

The new Project Map feature builds a visual representation of project systems using Git history and file interactions. This map helps connect related systems and brings relevant files into task briefs, allowing users to explore a system's tasks and plans before starting work.

Coordination is enhanced with sub-agents reporting results to their parent, an optional desk worker for stalled agents, and a Playbook for saving and reusing successful task recipes. Nested delegation can now go up to three levels deep.

The update also includes support for OpenCode, Claude Code, and OpenRouter as companion providers. Navigation is being reorganized around Home, Work, Live, and Models, with a unified queue for items needing attention.

AI assistance extends to project planning, with a partner that explores project files and offers editable suggestions backed by evidence. Quality-of-life improvements include clearer project preview controls and live appearance previews.

headline_marked: SpaceXAI [[aims for 1.44M GPUs]] by year-end, boosting AI power
headline: SpaceXAI aims for 1.44M GPUs by year-end, boosting AI power
summary: Elon Musk's AI venture is rapidly expanding its GPU capacity, with plans to reach 1.44 million units by the end of the year to power its AI ambitions.
details: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI is on track to significantly expand its AI infrastructure, aiming to have 1.44 million GPUs operational by the end of 2024. This massive deployment is part of a long-term vision to create a supercomputer capable of handling advanced AI tasks.

The expansion includes the addition of 660,000 new GPUs this year. Specifically, 220,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs are expected to be operational by next week, with another 220,000 by November, and a potential additional 220,000 by late December.

These new additions will supplement the existing GPUs in SpaceXAI's Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 data centers. Colossus 1 houses 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 GPUs, while Colossus 2 already has 110,000 GB200 and 440,000 GB300 GPUs.

The company is also addressing infrastructure challenges, particularly power supply. SpaceXAI is building its own 1.2 GW power plant to support the immense energy demands of its GPU clusters, a move that has led to some local controversies and lawsuits.

SpaceXAI's rapid growth places it among the leading AI companies, despite being younger than competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI. Musk has ambitious plans, aiming to increase data center capacity sevenfold by 2027 and targeting 50 million H100-equivalent GPUs by 2030, including potential orbital data centers.
